headline: Turkey Parliament Has a 65% Chance of Ratifying Mecca Joint Defence Agreement by 31 December
deck: Turkey submitted its 16-article pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan; an official parliamentary approval record by 31 December settles the 65% call.
body: Turkey has submitted the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement to parliament for ratification, opening a domestic approval process for the pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. [E3][E7] Al Jazeera, reporting on a document seen by Reuters, said the agreement was signed on 7 August, has 16 articles and aims to create a joint defence architecture if a member is attacked. [E8][E9] Reuters separately reported that Ankara was planning a mandate to send military personnel to Saudi Arabia; that report does not establish a parliamentary approval. [E1]

Submission is the first domestic gate, not the treaty’s operational result. Daily Sabah says the bill must go to a relevant parliamentary commission and the General Assembly, with any related military authorization also part of the process. [E5] The same outlet reported that opposition parties had pressed the government to seek parliamentary approval before implementing the alliance. [E4] Earlier, the three governments’ committee said practical collective-defence measures and rapid deployment of agreed forces and capabilities would proceed under each party’s national legislation. [E2] Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan had affirmed defence assistance to Saudi Arabia while ruling out Turkish troops’ active participation in the conflict between the Houthis and Saudis. [E6]

**The desk's reading.** The call is 65% that parliament ratifies the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement by 31 December 2026. The starting point is a neutral 50% prior because the record gives no commission schedule, vote count or amendment text. Submission and the governments’ stated collective-defence implementation move the probability upward. [E2][E3] The strongest competing reading is that the commission, Assembly and possible military-authorization stages create enough procedural and political friction to push a decision beyond the year; the opposition’s demand for approval makes that sequence consequential. [E4][E5] The filing therefore supports a modest edge for ratification, not certainty or an automatic deployment authority.

**The next test.** The call settles yes if an official Turkish parliamentary record shows approval of ratification by 31 December 2026. It settles no if parliament rejects or withdraws it, or if no official approval record is posted by 31 December 2026. A commission agenda, completed Assembly vote or published approval record would distinguish rapid ratification from procedural delay; a personnel mandate alone would not answer this call. [E1][E5]

confidence.label: Turkey's parliament ratifying the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement by 31 December 2026; NO if no official parliamentary approval record is posted by 31 December 2026.

dissent.argument: I put ratification by 31 December at 40%. The filing establishes submission, but not a commission calendar, vote count or published bill text. The remaining route runs through commission, General Assembly and potentially linked authorization; in a roughly ten-week window, that missing scheduling evidence outweighs the submission signal.
